International scholarships International Postgraduate Scholarship If you are starting a postgraduate degree at ARU, this scholarship can help with the costs of study. Value Up to £4,000, depending on qualifications Eligibility You should: be studying for an MBA or be an ARU graduate meet the eligibility criteria, including exceeding the minimum entry requirements Depending on the terms and conditions of your funding body, you may not be eligible if you are: sponsored by an organisation such as an employer, charitable body, or government department receiving federal tuition fee loans How to apply There is no need to apply. You will automatically receive our International Postgraduate Scholarship if you meet the eligibility criteria. You must meet all conditions of registration before the scholarship is awarded. If you withdraw from your course, we will adjust the scholarship on a pro-rata basis. Questions? Speak to our international team. Email [email protected] or call+44 1245 683680. How to apply Step 4 - Receive our decision on your application We aim to provide an initial response and/or a decision on your application as soon as possible. Provided you meet our English, academic and immigration requirements, you'll be likely to receive an offer from us. Accepting your offer If you applied to us directly, you need to accept your offer on your Applicant Portal within 28 days (or sooner depending on when you applied). You will receive instructions on how to access your Portal in your offer letter. If you applied to us through UCAS, you will need to accept your offer through UCAS Hub . You will need your UCAS Personal ID and password to log in, which UCAS will have provided to you when you applied. Deadlines apply so please refer to the UCAS website to check for the deadline to accept your offer. Meeting your conditions To meet the requirements of a conditional offer, you’ll need to provide copies of all documents requested (for example, academic qualifications and English language test results. You can upload all your required documents to your Applicant Portal. Sometimes, we may come back to you and ask for additional supporting documents. This will be communicated to you via your Applicant Portal and by email. Therefore, it's very important that the contact details on your application form are correct and up to date and that you check your email regularly for correspondence from us. Paying your deposit Aside from any academic conditions, you will also be asked to pay a deposit. Please note that all full fee paying international students will be required to pay a deposit before being issued with a CAS . Currently, the deposit for Undergraduate and Postgraduate taught courses is £4,000; further details will be included in your offer letter. Refunds of any deposit paid will be administered in accordance with the Rules, Regulations and Procedures for Students, which you will receive with your offer letter. A refund of a deposit may not be given in the event of a refusal of a visa arising from giving false or incomplete information to the United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI). To pay your deposit, as well as your fees, visit our fee payments page . Issuing your CAS Before we issue a CAS, you'll need to complete our Immigration History Form. You may also be asked to provide us with the documents you are going to use for your visa application. For more information about obtaining a CAS, please visit our immigration page . Once you receive your CAS, you'll be able to apply for your visa, although keep in mind that it will be issued no earlier than three months before the start date of your course . I haven't heard from you yet... Check your email, including the junk folder. We may have requested further information or additional documents from you. Contact your country representative or agent (if applicable). If you're a direct applicant and you haven’t heard from us in ten business days, please email [email protected] . Scholarships and bursaries Alumni Scholarship If you’ve already completed a degree at ARU and want to study a postgraduate course, this scholarship is for you. The Alumni Scholarship is a fee discount. We’ll deduct it from your tuition fees. Value There are two scholarships available: 20% off your fees if you achieved a 2:2 or above, and are applying for a postgraduate taught degree or a £400 discount if you're applying for a postgraduate research degree Duration The scholarship is awarded in the first year of the postgraduate taught or research degree (full-time) or across both years (part-time). Eligibility You should have completed one of the following: Full honours degree (BA/BSc, BEng, BOptom) Full Masters degree (MA/MSc, MEng) Postgraduate Certificate (PG Cert) Postgraduate Diploma (PG Dip) You must be: an ARU alumnus starting a new postgraduate taught or research award (in the first semester of study), either full-time or part-time starting your course in the 2026-27 academic year from the UK or an EU/EEA student who remains eligible for student finance . International students should see our International Alumni Scholarship . There's no time limit on when you completed your ARU award. Your award can be from predecessor institutions, or an ARU-validated degree at one of our partner institutions . This scholarship is not available for: degree apprenticeship or distance learning courses applicants who are receiving fee discounts from external agencies such as HEE, GMC or NMC MA Social Work students who receive the fee contribution from NHS Social Work Bursaries. How to apply There's no need to apply. You'll automatically be assessed for our Alumni Scholarship as part of your application. We’ll let you know if you’re eligible when we send you a conditional offer. Scholarships and bursaries Music Therapy Entry Bursary If you’re registered on our MA Music Therapy degree, this bursary can help pay for fees, books, living expenses and other costs during your training. The Music Therapy Entry Bursary is generously funded by the ARU Foundation Music Therapy Appeal and The Music Therapy Charity . Value Up to £1,000 (exact amount depends on the number of bursaries we award each round). Eligibility If you're registered for our MA Music Therapy degree you are eligible to apply for the bursary. If you have specific health or disability needs and/or are experiencing financial hardship, you will receive priority consideration for this bursary. How to apply Email a letter to the Course Director, Claire Molyneux , with the subject line Application for Entry Bursary 2026 . Your application letter should be no more than two A4 pages long, and must include the following details: your name and address a short summary of your aims and motivation for studying MA Music Therapy at ARU your current plans for funding the course, including details of other support, awards held or applied for, and donations how you intend to use the bursary your future plans and aspirations after you graduate from the course any specific health or disability needs, financial hardship or other matters that are relevant to your bursary application. When to apply Apply by 1 October in the first year of your Music Therapy degree. Other bursaries We offer a number of bursaries that you can apply for once you've started studying here. Two are for final-year MA Music Therapy students, and two for final-year MA Dramatherapy students. These bursaries support some of the activities you'll undertake as part of your training. Music Therapy Placement Travel and Clinical Supervision Bursary The Alice Zeitlyn Music Therapy Bursary The Ebb and Flow Dramatherapy Personal Therapy Bursary The Ebb and Flow Dramatherapy Placement Travel and Clinical Supervision Bursary We invite applications towards the end of Trimester 2, and you can apply at the start of Trimester 3 using an application form we'll share. Bursaries, and the amount awarded, are at the Course Director’s discretion and in line with the eligibility criteria outlined above. The Course Director’s decision is final and they reserve the right to not allocate the award or only partially allocate the award in any given year.
